scope: On-demand broader Physics. The public Physics edition collects four archives. Model and source trials are historical seven-day cohorts, not live operating days.
method: First and last five ranks per independent date. For exclusions with no accepted group and a successful review, assign the most frequent stored primary category, breaking ties alphabetically. Take the first five categories by SHA-256(date + space + category), then the first candidate in each by SHA-256(space-joined sorted paper IDs). A ranked case passes when the studies answer a comparable physical question and the dated text preserves their results and qualifications. An exclusion passes when fewer than three available studies support one specific comparable question. This is a single editorial assessment of a purposive sample, not an estimate of field-wide accuracy.
threshold: At least nine of ten passes in each of high, low and excluded across the two held-out weeks.

review.reason: All four theoretical batteries compare stored energy, charging or extractable work under a specified open-system model. The brief labels them as theory and the long text assigns the detuning limit and passive-energy bound to different models.

These studies ask how robust the DESI-era inference of evolving dark energy is to the model and additional dark-sector or neutrino freedom. The text assigns the simulated adequacy test, scalar-field mass bound and interacting-sector fits separately.

Two neural-basis studies approximate flow evolution. CoPiT predicts full aerodynamic fields, while the coarse-mesh study explicitly bypasses field reconstruction to predict sparse probes and integrated outputs. The text describes the different numerical benchmarks, but its member set lacks one comparable numerical objective.

Noise-induced heating in a levitated object, mode count in a cavity, magnon dissipation and electron decoherence near a metal do not measure the same loss observable. The brief does correctly identify three theoretical cavity studies and one electron experiment.

All three probe flat-band electronic structure in twisted graphene away from the usual magic angle. ARPES spectra at 2.4, 3.1 and 6.0 degrees are distinguished from the small-angle tunneling peak and its model-based heavy-fermion interpretation.

All three measure a change in star formation relative to a reference population or relation under a galaxy interaction or infall. The synthesis distinguishes dwarf radial profiles, matched major and minor mergers, and a satellite decline inferred using a proxy for infall time.

Neutrino direction and energy, cosmological parameter inference and jet tagging are distinct target quantities. The short summary extends cheap or unlabeled pretraining data and a scratch-training comparison across the group. SuperJEPA introduces a supervised objective and tests gains when large labeled samples already exist.

Muon trident production, deuteron spin asymmetries and neutrino-argon kinematic imbalance are three observables. The one-line forecast also blurs facilities: the first TeV measurement and Run 3 projection concern FASER; NA64mu extends the proposed energy-range comparison.

Each study investigates collective anisotropic flow in light-ion collisions, using overlapping flow coefficients or correlators. The text distinguishes ALICE measurements from the kinetic model tuned to them and the separate nonflow-corrected predictions.

Two studies reconstruct filaments or their connectivity in survey data. The ELUCID study measures local density, halo abundance and anisotropy relative to the tidal field. The dated text attributes the catalogue count, connectivity and simulated halo statistics individually.

A forest flux power spectrum, a CMB domain-wall signature, galaxy neighbor-count distributions, emission-line stacking and intrinsic alignments are distinct statistics. No three have the same measurement target.
Infrared properties of oxygen-rich giants, stellar radial-velocity multiplicity and the red wing of an interstellar absorption band require three separate interpretations.

Two papers examine diffuse radio emission linked to fossil plasma. The third measures the frequency of extreme scattering events from plasma lensing. The candidate falls short of three comparable papers.

The papers break into pairs concerning cosmological scalar or neutrino evolution, compact-object matter models, and black-hole perturbation or shadow calculations. No three establish the same observable in a specified system.

Oxygen elliptic flow and calcium/titanium flow calculations can be compared on selected quantities; the electric-charge fluctuation paper develops a separate equilibrium diagnostic. It does not make a third common flow study.

All five quantify QAOA solution quality or feasibility at specified resources. The short text generalizes the source of gains to classical choices. One hardware study measures noise-related retention of near-optima, and one encoding study finds a resource benefit without improved noiseless solution quality.

A memory threshold, logical-measurement fault distance, syndrome extraction on a silicon layout, and a qudit code's distance and frame errors answer distinct performance questions. The brief distinguishes the proofs from the two numerical results and retains the noise-model qualification.

The four formalisms target active-medium noise, nonlinear system–bath evolution, electron energy exchange and dissipative many-body spectra. No specified observable or model is shared across all four. The brief correctly places the results in theory.

The four releases follow the same Euclid DR1 galaxy-lens candidates from identification to modeling and property inference. The text retains candidate status, the denominators for model fits, and the assumptions behind the stellar masses. These companion papers are one survey program.

Three studies estimate the CMB optical depth, and an overlapping set of three calculates a 21-cm signal. The cosmic-ray heating paper does not estimate the optical depth and the kinetic SZ companion forecasts it without a 21-cm calculation. The text assigns the modeled quantities and conditional bounds correctly.

Only the honeycomb heterostructure study predicts Majorana corner modes from this specific altermagnet–superconductor setup. A separate study treats an altermagnet-induced higher-order insulator. A review surveys driven superconductors broadly. The brief presents Floquet phases as an extension of the same altermagnet proposal.

The three model families examine missing-energy B decays and specifically address the Belle II B-to-K plus missing-energy result. The text distinguishes which branching ratios constrain the vector-like quark, and which fits and bounds depend on a particular new-physics model.

The spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio can be compared across the inflation models. The repaired detailed summary specifies that the parity-odd metric-affine attractor is a separate theory. The headline and brief describe the entire group as corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which overstates that connection.

All three compare protected supersymmetric indices under proposed or established dualities. The short text distinguishes boundary half-indices from lens-space indices. The detailed text preserves the restriction to particular flat connections for even lens-space order.

The papers calculate when dynamical readouts can recover band-topology information, using Chern numbers or related invariants. The text keeps the isotropic-limit restriction on quantized spin transport with its chain and distinguishes quench and pump protocols.

Three papers involve charm, but pair-correlation production mechanisms, hadronic re-scattering spectra or elliptic flow, and higher flow harmonics do not yield a three-study comparison on one observable. The remaining papers measure jet or temperature observables.

Cascade-rate estimators, driven magnetosonic structures, solar-wind wave refraction, a heliosphere framework, stellar oscillation suppression, stellar wind loss and shock acceleration use different response quantities and environments.
Galaxy flexion, an instrumental contaminant of HI intensity maps, robustness of a galaxy BAO-peak estimate and CMB polarization delensing do not measure one shared observable.

Two domain-wall studies could motivate a paired comparison, but the remaining papers treat skyrmion merger textures and the orientation of a driven slender particle. There is no third domain-wall measurement.

The M-dwarf radio observation and stellar-wind models both concern star–planet environments. The independent white-dwarf merger fraction and mass limit have a different target. The three-paper minimum is not met.

native_sampling: October: three primary entries per archive in the October monthly listings in SHA-256(versionless ID) order whose separate v1 page dates the paper to October 22–28. November: eligible entries from the previously frozen 12-example November sample. Both methods use the official arXiv listing, independent of the stored candidate selection.
cost_method: Subtract the parent store model ledger for a rerun, and use the whole ledger for a cold week. Month keys refer to the actual time of processing. Model charges in this comparison do not project a platform monthly ceiling.
